architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent repeats. Accept the reactive-core baseline as consistent with H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 is between 7.51% and 11.51% inclusive, corresponding to the 9.51% linear-dilution prediction plus or minus the declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination resolution, and the repeat values differ by no more than 2.00 percentage points.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-CORE at the declared resolution if the mean SI_15_60 across the independent repeats is below 7.51%, which is more than 2.00 percentage points below the 9.51% prediction. A mean at or above 11.51% is non-confirmatory but does not by itself falsify H-CORE. No result from this core-only composition can falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL because neither modifier axis is active.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the matched reactive-mass-fraction hold set recommended by the Skeptic: the S1C02 reactive-core control, an acrylic-only composition with 15-20% AC1920 and TK100 = 0, and a tackifier-active composition with TK100 near 5%, using controlled and fully recorded preparation histories, at least two repeats per composition, and the same 120 C 15-60 min hold.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over 15-60 min
judge_normalized.rationale: Among the supplied experiment cards, S1C02::M-HOLD-120 is the least extrapolative direct test of the reactive-core reference at the least-resolved coordinate. It is scientifically defensible only as a baseline control for H-CORE, not as a standalone adjudication of modifier mechanisms. Its numeric criteria are restricted accordingly.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic over the Proposer on hypothesis interpretation: S1C02 cannot test H-RESIN or H-DUAL, and the proposer's multi-hypothesis falsification language was removed. I followed the Robustness Adjudicator in retaining S1C02 only as the available reactive-core control, because the payload does not provide identifiers for the recommended acrylic-only and tackifier-active candidates. The direct hold was retained over M-REPEAT because the declared failure mode is 120 C viscosity drift, not viscosity-scale spread.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged residence of the 120 C melt, with the magnitude of drift potentially depending on modifier chemistry rather than reactive-core dilution alone.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C thermal holds show SI_15_60 of 0.515 (51.54%) for E5 versus 0.095 (9.51%) for E1, with E5 reaching SI_15_90 of 0.931 (93.08%).
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local hold evidence contains only E1 and E5, each with one original run and four observations over 15-90 minutes. It therefore establishes a large endpoint contrast but poorly resolves the trajectory across composition and modifier axes; no follow-up hold profiles are measured. Temperature response has six-point sweeps from 80-130 C, while realized viscosity level has descriptive repeat data for E2, although that level also shows substantial 2.80-3.57x spread.
measurement_requirements: Measure matched-window 120 C thermal holds at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report SI_15_60 directly without extrapolation.
Use at least two independent repeats per composition with fully recorded preparation and thermal history.
Compare an acrylic-only composition, a composition with a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction, and an appropriate reactive-core or dilution reference at matched reactive mass fraction.
Measure and report the realized viscosity level and temperature response over the supported range so drift differences are not confounded by uncontrolled process state or unsupported extrapolation.
Preserve the full time trajectories, not only the final endpoint, to distinguish linear dilution, superlinear suppression, and tackifier-required behavior.
planner.scientific_question: At matched process state and comparable reactive mass fraction, does modifier chemistry reduce 120 C isothermal viscosity drift beyond linear dilution, and does achieving the low-drift regime require the minor tackifier-like axis rather than the acrylic-like axis alone?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE: a reactive-core-only composition gives the same linear-dilution drift prediction as the other hypotheses at reactive mass fraction 1.0, so this experiment cannot distinguish it from H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
H-RESIN: no resin-modified composition is tested, so resin-specific superlinear suppression cannot be established.
H-DUAL: no acrylic-like or minor-tackifier-like axis is active, so tackifier-required behavior cannot be tested.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 4.75% across at least two repeats, the reactive-core baseline is substantially below its 9.51% linear-dilution reference and H-CORE is falsified at this resolution. This would not by itself establish H-RESIN, because no resin modifier was tested.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 9.51%, H-RESIN's suppression prediction is not supported by this baseline and H-CORE remains consistent with the observed core drift. A value between 4.75% and 9.51% would weaken the stated binary discrimination because it is below the linear prediction but not below the card's half-prediction threshold.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: An intermediate result, especially one between 4.75% and 9.51%, indicates that the reactive-core reference is not cleanly classified by the registered thresholds. Repeat-to-repeat spread and the full 15-30-45-60 minute trajectory must be retained before attributing the difference to modifier chemistry.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has the same deterministic component vector and direct hold observable, but is a less central reactive-core perturbation than the explicitly designated E2 anchor.
It is another reactive-core-only perturbation with identical hypothesis discrimination and no active modifier axis, offering no additional separation of H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
It better controls realization state but measures viscosity-scale spread rather than the registered isothermal drift coordinate, so it cannot directly adjudicate the failure-mode hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: Among the supplied tied hold cards, S1C02 is the most scientifically defensible baseline because E2 is the characterized geometric-centre reactive-core anchor and has documented realization-state uncertainty. The direct 120 C matched-window hold addresses the least-resolved coordinate without model inference. However, this is a baseline characterization experiment, not a strong intervention-discrimination experiment: with both modifier axes zero, none of the registered hypothesis pairs is actually separated.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C02 uses the explicitly identified E2 reactive-core anchor, the geometric centre of the original local design, and is therefore the least perturbed baseline for interpreting later modifier comparisons. The matched-window hold reads drift directly without a model fit or extrapolation.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Retain S1C02::M-HOLD-120 only as the E2 reactive-core control, and expand the experiment to a matched set including acrylic-only and minor-tackifier-active compositions. Do not interpret the S1C02 result alone as separating H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
residual_decision_risk: The payload does not provide the candidate identifiers for the required acrylic-only and tackifier-active matched compositions.
Process-state variation remains a major confounder; E2 previously showed up to a 3.57x realized-viscosity ratio at 120 C.
At least two repeats are specified, but the supplied proposal lacks a complete rule for combining discordant repeat results.
The matched-window hold directly measures drift, but the hypotheses may remain unresolved if the observed differences are within the declared 2.0 percentage-point discrimination threshold.
Decision stability is unavailable because the deterministic perturbation sweep was withheld.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C02 has no active modifier axis, so it cannot adjudicate H-RESIN or H-DUAL, and its stated H-RESIN falsification criterion is invalid. The experiment remains useful only as the E2 reactive-core control. The scientifically appropriate action is to run it as part of a matched reactive-mass-fraction set that also includes an acrylic-only composition and a tackifier-active composition, with controlled and recorded preparation history and a predefined repeat-level decision rule.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 is in the deterministic tied top set. The supplied payload withholds the decision-stability sweep, including top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary, so no specific weight perturbations or defensibility of such perturbations can be assessed.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The primary observable SI_15_60 is directly measurable under M-HOLD-120, and the H-CORE threshold of 4.75% is separated from the 9.51% prediction by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. However, the full stated falsification criterion cannot be met for H-RESIN or H-DUAL because no active modifier axis is tested and the H-DUAL wording incorrectly calls the zero-modifier composition acrylic-only. The criterion is therefore not attainable as a multi-hypothesis adjudication, even though a limited H-CORE baseline check is feasible.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A measured drift cannot identify resin-specific superlinear suppression or tackifier-required behavior; it can at most test whether this reactive-core realization is inconsistent with the 9.51% H-CORE reference.
objections.objection: The selected S1C02 formulation has AC1920 = 0.0% and TK100 = 0.0%, with reactive mass fraction 1.0. Consequently, the registered predictions for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL all collapse to 9.51%, exactly as shown in hypothesis_discrimination_detail. The experiment leaves all three hypotheses entangled rather than separating any pair. The proposer admits this in hypotheses_not_separated, but the acceptance language still claims possible H-RESIN-over-H-CORE discrimination.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Results at or above 9.51% would not falsify H-RESIN, and a low result would not establish or properly falsify H-DUAL. The proposed decision rule would overstate what the protocol can reject.
objections.objection: The stated falsification criterion says H-RESIN is falsified if the S1C02 core-only drift is at or above 9.51%. That is not the registered H-RESIN falsification condition, which requires a resin-modified composition to remain at or above the linear-dilution prediction. No resin-modified composition is measured. Likewise, the criterion says H-DUAL is falsified if 'this acrylic-only composition' reaches the low-drift regime, but S1C02 is not acrylic-only: both modifier axes are zero.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A departure from 9.51% could be attributed to core or preparation differences, weakening even the intended H-CORE baseline test and preventing clean attribution to modifier chemistry in any later comparison.
objections.objection: Although the two modifier axes do not move together in S1C02, the comparison baseline is the single original E1 hold with SI_15_60 = 9.51%, whereas S1C02 uses the distinct E2 reactive-core composition. Thus any difference from 9.51% can reflect reactive-core composition, stoichiometric details, or realization state rather than the registered modifier mechanisms. The protocol also does not control process state, and E2 showed a 3.57x maximum-to-minimum viscosity ratio at 120 C across three preparations.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may produce a direct SI_15_60 value but still fail to yield a reproducible, pre-specified H-CORE decision when the repeats disagree.
objections.objection: The H-CORE threshold itself is measurable: 4.75% is 4.76 percentage points below the 9.51% prediction and therefore exceeds the declared 2.00% resolution. However, the protocol specifies only 'at least two independent repeats' and gives no rule for how repeat variability is combined or how a result is judged when one repeat is below and one is above 4.75%. Given the documented uncontrolled state risk, the phrase 'across at least two repeats' is not a complete operational falsification rule.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the single S1C02 hold with a matched reactive-mass-fraction set containing the E2 reactive-core control, an acrylic-only composition with AC1920 in the supported 15-20% band and TK100 = 0, and a tackifier-active composition with TK100 near 5% (with the reactive core recalculated for any reactive functionality). Run the same direct 15-60 min holds with controlled and fully recorded preparation history, at least two repeats per composition, and predefine the repeat-level decision rule.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The stated criterion that S1C02 can falsify H-RESIN at SI_15_60 >= 9.51% is invalid: H-RESIN requires a resin-modified composition for adjudication, but S1C02 has AC1920 = 0.0% and TK100 = 0.0%.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
